why: The answer correctly says that a successful javac leaves a Big.class file and prints nothing because the program has not been run yet; this is the compile result, not a relational explanation of how javac and java link together.

concepts.quote: There is a Big.class file now, but nothing is printed
concepts.why: A successful compile creates Big.class and produces no program output, which is exactly the compile result.

concepts.quote: because the program has not run yet
concepts.why: It notes that running is a separate step that has not happened, but does not explain that java Big runs the Big.class that javac made.

concepts.quote: There is a Big.class file now, but nothing is printed because the program has not run yet
concepts.why: It matches the rule that the program text's result is Big.class and output appears only when the program is run.
The answer makes no claim about the class declaration or the class name.
